svg.title: HTTP filter query pipeline
svg.desc: An HTTP request's filter, orFilter and sort parameters are untrusted client input. HttpFilterParser reads each condition as field:operator[:value] and applies the limits set with the specrepository.http properties: max-filters (default 20, conditions in filter and orFilter together), max-sort-fields (5), max-values-per-filter (100 values of an in or notin filter), max-value-length (1000 characters) and allowed-operators (empty means every registered operator). A malformed expression, an invalid field name or a limit exceeded throws HttpFilterSyntaxException; an operator outside allowed-operators throws HttpUnknownOperatorException. The parser produces a QueryPlan of client conditions and sort that carries an AllowedFieldsPolicy, which denies by default and matches exact names. With @FilterableQuery, its argument resolver validates the plan against it at this point, before the handler runs: a field outside the lists throws DisallowedFieldException, and a @FilterableQuery without a list for that usage throws UndeclaredFieldListException. A plan built with toQueryPlan is not checked by the parser: it is checked at execution, unless the application calls policy.validate(plan) first. Server conditions such as a tenant check come from code, added with repository.query(plan).where(...); they are combined as (client conditions) AND (server conditions), so a filter cannot widen them, and the policy does not apply to them. When the query runs, the repository checks a Pageable sort against the sortable fields, and QueryPlanSpecificationFactory.create(plan) checks the policy again, resolves the fields on the JPA metamodel, picks each operator's OperatorHandler and converts the values, producing a Specification; an unknown field or an operator without a handler throws InvalidFilterException, a value that cannot be converted throws InvalidFilterValueException, and a field that the policy re-check rejects, or a Pageable sort outside the sortable fields, throws DisallowedFieldException. The Specification becomes SQL with every value bound as a JDBC parameter and LIKE wildcards escaped. Every rejection happens before any SQL runs: HttpFilterProblemDetailsExceptionHandler answers it with 400 Bad Request and an application/problem+json body whose detail is the exception message and whose field property names the field when the exception has one, as the SpecrepoInvalidFilter response describes, also when a repository proxy wraps the exception in InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException. The animation follows a valid request to SQL, then requests rejected by the parser, by the allow-list and while the Specification is built.
